study_design: Population-based case-control study conducted in Auckland, New Zealand.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: A population-based case-control study was conducted in Auckland, New Zealand, involving 317 prostate cancer cases and 480 controls.
reason: The abstract evaluates prostate cancer risk overall and does not report an aggressive, advanced, metastatic, high-grade, high-risk, or lethal prostate cancer endpoint.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Increasing levels of MUFA-rich vegetable oil intake were associated with a progressive reduction in prostate cancer risk (multivariate relative risk = 0.5; 95% confidence interval 0.3-0.9; > 5.5 ml per day vs. nonconsumption, p trend = 0.005), and similar trends were observed across all strata of socioeconomic status.
estimate_classifications.reason: The estimate concerns overall prostate cancer risk without an aggressive disease restriction.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Prostate cancer risk was not associated with intake of total MUFA or the major animal food sources of MUFA.
estimate_classifications.reason: The abstract reports a total-MUFA association with overall prostate cancer risk but supplies no numeric effect and confidence interval.
